audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagreed with the packet chart and with the already-audited mirror (mel__sett).
audit.why: Packet chart is Mel/Skill/Sett/Sett/Sett/Sett/Sett; the mirror agreed to flip Levels 4-5 to Skill and First item to Mel while keeping Level 3 and Level 6 for Sett. Current rows read Skill/Skill/Skill/Mel/Skill/Mel/Mel, which contradicts both and the 60.83% win rate.
audit.corrected: Mel / Skill / Sett / Skill / Sett / Mel / Sett, proposed as matched full+content pairs with ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text asserted Rebuttal 'parries' Sett's R and gave no Golden Eclipse threat.
audit.why: Riot text for Rebuttal (W, 38/35/33/29/26s) says it reflects enemy projectiles and prevents her taking damage — none of Sett's abilities are projectiles, so nothing is reflected. Golden Eclipse (R, 120/100/80s) is the real spike: it strikes from any range and scales off Overwhelm stacks.
audit.corrected: Spike 2 now states the barrier blocks damage and reflects projectiles; spike 3 now states Overwhelm/Golden Eclipse threshold behaviour.

audit.whatIsWrong: Facebreaker described as a root that always lands a stun; Sett's Grit-from-poke interaction absent; Mel referred to as 'he'.
audit.why: Facebreaker (E, 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s) pulls enemies on OPPOSITE sides and only stuns then — one-sided pulls slow instead. Sett's W banks damage taken as Grit, so Radiant Volley poke feeds Haymaker's true-damage centre. Mel is female.
audit.corrected: Text now states the both-sides stun condition, the poke-into-Grit conversion, and correct pronouns.

audit.why: Solar Snare is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s — concrete numbers make the engage window actionable.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now carries the real range.

edits.before: He kites your hands — hold W for his commit and E-stun the moment he steps to poke. Sett wins by trading around Mel's Solar Snare and cashing the pattern: bank grit, land the E-stun, cash the W panel.
edits.after: She kites your hands, but every Radiant Volley you eat is banked Grit for Haymaker's true-damage centre. Trade around Solar Snare, land the E-stun with her boxed in, then cash the W panel.

edits.before: He kites your hands — hold W for his commit and E-stun the moment he steps to poke.
edits.after: She kites your hands — hold W until her poke banks Grit, then E-stun when she steps up.

edits.before: E-stun him when Solar Snare is down
edits.after: E-stun her when Solar Snare is down

edits.before: - Mel Solar Snare: matchup-defining — Her root / slow zone — sets up her combo. Dodge it. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Mel Solar Snare (E): 11s at rank 1, 9s at rank 5 — her root and slow zone. Bait it, then engage inside that window.

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Mel on every CS, but respect her opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Radiant Volley reaches 950 units and chips you from behind her wave, so level 1 is hers. Soak XP, bank the Grit her poke hands you, and save the commit for Facebreaker.

edits.before: Facebreaker is online — the E-stun into double punch + W is your full pattern. Run it the moment Mel burns Solar Snare.
edits.after: Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on both sides — pull her across your minions, double-punch, cash W once Solar Snare is down.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Mel. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before she matches your item.
edits.after: Her first item lands first and Radiant Volley starts to hurt. Stridebreaker fixes your sticking problem — shove, recall on the spike, force the trade back.

edits.before: Level 3 E Facebreaker roots her out of her kite and wins the trade.
edits.after: Level 3 Facebreaker pulls her in and stuns if she is boxed in.

edits.before: Through levels 4-5 your Q-W combo deletes her squishy mage body.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 hinge on Solar Snare — dodge it and Q-W wins the trade.

edits.before: Respect her W Rebuttal reflect — don't dump R The Show Stopper into an active parry; wait it out, then all-in for a near-guaranteed kill.
edits.after: Rebuttal (W) blocks all damage while it holds and reflects projectiles back — wait the barrier out, then commit The Show Stopper for the kill.

edits.before: Your bruiser first item plus Pit Grit sustain lets you walk her poke and one-combo her; at 60%+ win rate the all-in is overwhelming.
edits.after: Overwhelm stacks on every hit she lands and Golden Eclipse cashes them from any range — watch the HP number, not the bar, and reset early.

notes: Mel's Rebuttal carries a 'terrain' derived flag, but Riot's description says only that it forms a barrier around her that reflects projectiles, prevents damage and grants move speed — no terrain is created. Treated the flag as a tooltip-parse misfire and did not write the _missing 'terrain-cuts-retreat' line. Whether Sett's The Show Stopper can grab her during Rebuttal is not answerable from Riot text (damage prevention is stated, untargetability is not), so no claim was made either way — logged in unverified. Level chart aligned to the packet plus the mirror's two agreed flips; all five changed rows proposed as matched full+content pairs.
